title: 5 · Timestamp Ordering & Log-Based Recovery (Unit 3)
learn:
Timestamp ordering

The DBMS gives each transaction a unique timestamp TS(Ti) (system clock or a logical counter), so an older transaction has a smaller TS. Each item A keeps RTS(A), the largest timestamp that read it successfully, and WTS(A), the largest timestamp that wrote it.

Read(A) by Ti: if WTS(A) > TS(Ti) then rollback Ti; else execute and set RTS(A) = max(RTS(A), TS(Ti)).
Write(A) by Ti: if RTS(A) > TS(Ti) rollback; if WTS(A) > TS(Ti) rollback; else execute and set WTS(A) = TS(Ti).

Worked example: T1=10, T2=20, T3=30. After T3 reads A the RTS is 30; T2's later read leaves it at 30. Writes by T1 (10) then T4 (40) give WTS(A) = 40.

Recovery management

Recovery restores the database to the most recent consistent state before a failure. Failure types: system crash, transaction (logical) error, concurrency-control enforcement, local errors, disk failure, physical problems or catastrophes.

Log records

[start_transaction, T], [write_item, T, X, old, new], [read_item, T, X], [commit, T], [abort, T].

Deferred update (no-undo/redo): the physical database changes only after the commit point. Committed: redo. Not committed: ignore/rollback.
Immediate update (undo/redo): the database changes during execution. Failure before commit: undo using old values. Committed: redo using new values.

Deferred vs immediate at a glance

Deferred (no-undo/redo): log is written first, disk changes only after commit, so nothing to undo; committed work is redone. Immediate (undo/redo): disk may change before commit; uncommitted work is undone using the old value, committed work is redone using the new value.

quiz.q: Read by Ti is rolled back when?
quiz.why: A younger transaction already wrote it.

quiz.q: A write by Ti is rolled back when?
Deferred update changes the database when?
A log record with old and new values supports?
quiz.why: Old for undo, new for redo.

lab.task: A has RTS=0, WTS=0. T1 (TS 100) writes A, then T2 (TS 50) reads A. What happens?
lab.solution: T1's write sets WTS(A)=100. T2 reads with WTS(A)=100 > TS(T2)=50, so T2 is rolled back.
